^.what: The start of the text, or of each line with m.

$.what: The end of the text, or of each line with m.

\\b.what: A word boundary: between a \w and what is not one.

\\B.what: Anywhere but at a word boundary.

\\A.what: The start of the text only, even with m.

\\z.what: The end of the text only, even with m.

\\Z.what: The end of the text, or just before a final line break.

\\G.what: Where the previous match ended; JavaScript has the y flag instead.

..what: Any character but a line break; line breaks included with s.

\\w.what: A word character: an ASCII letter, a digit or an underscore.

\\s.what: Whitespace: a space, a tab, a line break…

[abc].what: One of the characters in the set (character class).

[^abc].what: A character not in the set (negated class).

\\p{L}.what: A character with a Unicode property: L letter, N number, Script=Greek…

\\P{L}.what: A character without the Unicode property.

[[:alpha:]].what: A POSIX class, inside brackets: alpha, digit, space, upper…

\\h.what: Horizontal whitespace: a space or a tab, never a line break.

\\R.what: Any line break: CR LF, LF or CR.

\\X.what: A whole grapheme: a letter and its accents, a composed emoji.

*.what: Zero times or more, as many as possible (greedy).

+.what: Once or more, as many as possible.

?.what: Zero times or once: makes it optional.

*?.what: As few as possible (lazy); likewise +?, ?? and {n,m}?.

*+.what: As many as possible, never giving any back (possessive); likewise ++ and ?+.

(…).what: A capturing group, numbered from the left: $1, $2…

(?:…).what: A group that does not capture (non-capturing), to group alone.

(?<name>…).what: A named group, read back by its name.

\\k<name>.what: The text a named group captured.

(?>…).what: An atomic group: once left, it never backtracks into it.

(?i:…).what: A flag for this group alone (modifier).

(?i).what: A flag for the rest of the pattern.

(?R).what: The whole pattern, called again (recursion): nested parentheses.

m.what: Multiline: ^ and $ hold for each line.

s.what: The dot takes line breaks too (dotAll).

g.what: Every match, not only the first (global); in PCRE, the caller loops.

u.what: Read the text as Unicode: an emoji is one character.
u.pcre: (*UTF) at the start of the pattern

v.what: Unicode with set operations inside brackets: -- and && (unicodeSets).

x.what: Ignore the pattern's whitespace and allow # comments (extended).

n.what: Parentheses no longer capture, but named groups.

\\xhh.what: The character of this hexadecimal code, in two digits.

\\uhhhh.what: The character of this UTF-16 code, in four digits.

\\cX.what: The control character Ctrl+X: \cJ is a line feed.
